title: Operadic algebroids and their complete objects
statement:
Use the simplicial sets and simplex category of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], and the quasicategories, spaces, mapping spaces, coherent functors, transformations and full subcategories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$; small means $\mathcal U$-small, and all categories under discussion fit in $\mathcal U'$. Use the fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] and a monoidal infinity category $p:\mathcal V^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ with tensor unit $\mathbf1$ and inert maps as in [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category].

For a small space $X$ represented by a Kan complex, define the strict simplicial-set-valued functor $F_X$ on $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ by $F_X([n])=X^{n+1}$ and $F_X(\alpha)((x_0,\ldots,x_n))=(x_{\alpha^{\mathrm{op}}(0)},\ldots,x_{\alpha^{\mathrm{op}}(m)})$ for $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$. Specify $\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ by the relative nerve of $F_X$: an $r$-simplex consists of a functor $\sigma:[r]\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ and, for every nonempty subset $J\subseteq[r]$, a simplicial map $t_J:\Delta^J\to F_X(\sigma(\max J))$, satisfying $t_J|_{\Delta^I}=F_X(\sigma(\max I)\to\sigma(\max J))t_I$ for $\varnothing\ne I\subseteq J$. Here $\Delta^J$ is the simplex on the ordered set $J$, the projection remembers $\sigma$, and for an order-preserving $\theta:[r\prime]\to[r]$ the induced simplicial operator sends $(\sigma,t)$ to $(\sigma\circ\theta,t\prime)$ with $t\prime_J=t_{\theta(J)}\circ(\theta|_J):\Delta^J\to\Delta^{\theta(J)}\to F_X(\sigma(\max\theta(J)))$ for every nonempty $J\subseteq[r\prime]$. Each $X^{n+1}$ is Kan: fill any horn independently in each coordinate. By [lem-coef-kan-relative-nerve-left-fibration], this is the specified left-fibration model for the space-valued functor $[n]\mapsto X^{n+1}$.

A $\mathcal V$-algebroid with object space $X$ is a coherent functor $A:\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ sending inert edges to $p$-cocartesian edges; an edge in the domain is inert when it is cocartesian over an inert base map. Write $A(x,y)$ for its value over $(x,y)\in X^2$ in the fiber over $[1]$. The fiber category $\operatorname{Alg}_X(\mathcal V)$ is the full subcategory of functors over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ on these objects. A map of spaces $f:X\to Y$ gives $f^*B$ by precomposition with the induced map $\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}\to\Delta_Y^{\mathrm{op}}$. Write $\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal V)$ for the total infinity category of $X\mapsto\operatorname{Alg}_X(\mathcal V)$: a morphism from $(X,A)$ to $(Y,B)$ consists of $f:X\to Y$ and a morphism $A\to f^*B$ in $\operatorname{Alg}_X(\mathcal V)$, with higher simplices retaining their coherent compatibilities; composition uses precomposition and composition of these transformations.

For the discrete object space $\{0,\ldots,n\}$, $E^n$ is the algebroid whose mapping objects are all $\mathbf1$, with unit and composition maps the unit constraints. Maps of these finite sets give a cosimplicial object $E^\bullet$. Put $\iota_n A=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal V)}(E^n,A)$, a simplicial space by precomposition, and let $\iota A:=\operatorname{colim}_{[n]\in\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}\iota_n A$ in spaces. Complete means that the canonical map $\iota_0 A\to\iota A$ is an equivalence. Write $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal V}$ for the full subcategory of complete algebroids. A morphism $A\to B$ over $f:X\to Y$ is fully faithful when every $A(x,y)\to B(fx,fy)$ is an equivalence in $\mathcal V$. It is essentially surjective when $\pi_0(\iota A)\to\pi_0(\iota B)$ is surjective; here $\pi_0$ denotes components of a space.

Presentable has the meaning of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Presentably monoidal means that the underlying infinity category is presentable and tensoring with any fixed object preserves all small colimits in each variable.
